newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom gains right to U.S. facilities.
newsitem.headline: Telecom gains right to U.S. facilities.

text.p: Telecom Corp of New Zealand said it had gained the right to set up its own facilities in the United States after passing a competition test with the Federal Communications Commission (FCC).

"At the moment we are simply transiting traffic through the United States to other destinations, but we are now allowed legally to have our own facilities in the United States if we wish and it seemed sensible to take up that right," Telecom general manager of network marketing Anthony Briscoe said.
Telecom spokesman Clive Litt said Telecom currently routes telephone traffic through the United States via other carriers, and there were no current plans to change this as a result of the approval.
Telecom was the first company ever to seek the approval from the FCC. The United States last year announced a programme to deregulate its telecommunications market.

The FCC found that New Zealand's telecommunications market met the four key criteria of legal ability to enter, terms and conditions of interconnection, competitive safeguards and the regulatory framework for U.S. facilities-based carriers
